verdict.rationale: Bolt documents iterative prompting with safeguards: Plan Mode lets you plan without changing code, and GitHub sync keeps a full history of changes. One user reports building apps with 99% of edits made through prompts by reverting bad attempts. But concrete hands-on reports contradict the 'without breaking what works' part: one user says the AI made unauthorized changes that removed a security layer and killed payment functionality, and another describes a 'doom loop' where each fix resurrected a previous break. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of change isolation or regression protection for follow-up prompts, a documented in-product revert/checkpoint feature, consistent hands-on evidence that existing functionality survives iteration.

support.subject: As a founder, I can refine my app through follow-up prompts without breaking what already works

citations.quote: Bolt has a chat mode called Plan Mode where you can plan and ask questions without making changes to your code.
Connecting GitHub to Bolt lets you automatically back up your Bolt project with a full history of changes that lives outside Bolt.
both were built in bolt with 99% of edits made through prompts
